job.title: Chair (Renumerated | Lived Experience Identified)
job.description:
The Organisation 

The National Mental Health Consumer Alliance (Alliance) believes people with lived and living experience must shape the decisions that affect their lives. 

Australia's national peak body for mental health consumers, the Alliance is a federation of state and territory consumer peaks, led by and for people with lived and living experience. They carry the voices of consumers and survivors into national policy and reform, guided by the values of frank and robust collaboration, challenging the status quo, supporting diversity of experience and expertise, and openness and equity. 

The Role 

Elected by the Board as an independent Director, the Chair will lead the Alliance Board into its next chapter, keeping the federation united around a shared purpose and true to lived experience values. 

The successful candidate will help shape how the Board and CEO build a trusted partnership, how strategy and performance frameworks stay focused, and how consumer and survivor voices are carried with unity into national reform. You will lead constructive Board meetings, oversee financial sustainability and risk, and guide Board performance, CEO review and succession planning. 

As the Board's representative, you will build trust across the state and territory peaks and with Government, alongside the CEO. 

The Candidate Profile 

This is a renumerated position, and the candidate can be based anywhere in Australia.

The Alliance is seeking a collaborative Chair who connects people around a shared purpose, builds trust and alignment through influence, and develops an open, honest partnership with the CEO, while maintaining the important distinction between governance and operational leadership. 

The ideal candidate will bring Board experience and sound governance knowledge, with Chair experience highly regarded but not essential. Experience in a federated, membership-based peak body or similarly complex environment, financial literacy and skilled facilitation will be valued. Formal governance qualifications are not required. 

Having a lived/living experience of mental distress as a consumer (rather than as a carer or supporter) is essential. Knowledge of the consumer and survivor movement will be highly regarded. Most importantly, the successful candidate will be guided by lived experience values and committed to amplifying consumer and survivor voices in national reform. 

Our approach to lived experience and inclusive recruitment
  
We recognise lived and living experience as valuable expertise and are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is inclusive, respectful, accessible and trauma-informed.
  
Candidates are not expected or required to disclose personal details of their lived or living experience, including diagnoses, treatment histories or traumatic experiences, in their cover letter, application or during the recruitment and interview process.
  
We are interested in understanding the perspectives, insights and leadership expertise candidates bring through their lived or living experience, rather than the personal circumstances of those experiences.
  
We respect each candidate's choice about what they share and welcome conversations about any adjustments or support that may assist their participation.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
About The Walkley Foundation

The Walkley Foundation exists to celebrate and support great Australian journalism in order to strengthen our democracy. They are the custodians of excellence in reporting in Australia, working collaboratively with all journalists and media organisations to encourage ethical, best-practice journalism. Part of its mission is to create a community of journalists.

First presented in 1956 by the Australian Journalists Association – the forerunner of MEAA – the Walkley Awards are Australia’s benchmark for excellence in journalism. The Foundation works with all journalists and media organisations to recognise great journalism, lift the craft through professional development, and invest in journalism through scholarships, fellowships and grants.

The Role

Reporting directly to the Board, the Chief Executive Officer will lead the Walkley Foundation into its next chapter, developing and delivering a new strategy that builds on its proud legacy while creating a more sustainable future.
The CEO will:
  • Lead the development and delivery of a new strategic plan with the Board.
  • Strengthen and diversify revenue across sponsorship, partnerships, philanthropy, grants and earned income.
  • Grow professional development, training and other opportunities that lift the craft of journalism and build community amongst journalists.
  • Lead a small, committed team, balancing strategic leadership with hands-on operational and financial oversight.
  • Build trusted relationships across journalists, MEAA, the Judging Board, partners, funders and the broader media community.
  • Act as a credible public voice for the Foundation, championing great Australian journalism and its role in a strong democracy
  • Sydney is the preferred location, with candidates based elsewhere in Australia also considered. Hybrid working is available.
The Candidate Profile

The Walkley Foundation is seeking a courageous, commercially astute leader who combines strategic vision with a hands-on, delivery-focused approach. The ideal candidate brings the financial acumen, judgement and energy to set a clear direction, drive change and build a vibrant, sustainable organisation, while fostering a cohesive, high-performing team culture.

The ideal candidate will bring senior leadership experience working closely with Boards, with CEO experience highly regarded, together with strong capability across strategy, financial management, commercial partnerships, sponsorship and revenue growth. A compelling, authentic communicator with proven media ability, they will be confident as the face of the organisation and in building relationships with media organisations, journalists, partners, donors, government and MEAA.

An understanding of the media industry and the future of journalism is important. Experience within member-based organisations, professional associations, unions, the arts or media will be highly regarded, and leaders from across the not-for-profit sector are encouraged to apply. Most importantly, the successful candidate will understand why journalism matters, share a deep commitment to independent, ethical journalism, and align with the values of MEAA as custodian of the Foundation.
